description: Figure 3 is a horizontal bar chart that illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) between two fine-tuned models — the NESAC ft model (orange bars) and the SESHA ft model (green bars) — and the Whisper large-v3 model, after applying a sequence of cumulative automated post-processing optimisation steps. The vertical axis lists five optimisation categories: “Normalised,” “Add Spacing,” “Remove Spacing,” “Americanisms,” and “Dates,” arranged from top to bottom, indicating that each subsequent step includes all prior optimisations. The horizontal axis, labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” ranges from 0.000 to 0.0035 and quantifies the reduction in WER relative to Whisper large-v3. Each bar is labeled with its precise numerical value: for “Normalised,” the NESAC ft model shows a difference of 0.00334 and SESHA ft model 0.00323; for “Add Spacing,” 0.00319 and 0.00344 respectively; for “Remove Spacing,” 0.00311 and 0.00306; for “Americanisms,” 0.00299 and 0.00302; and for “Dates,” 0.00257 and 0.00228. A legend below the chart identifies the orange bars as representing the NESAC ft model and the green bars as the SESHA ft model. The chart visually demonstrates that both fine-tuned models consistently outperform Whisper large-v3 across all optimisation stages, with the performance gap narrowing as more optimisations are applied.
